Scouting Summary

Common themes

  • Right Fast, averaging 139.6 kph (up to 146.0).
  • Typical length is 7-8m (their good length); median 7.6 m.
  • Stock ball is a good length wide outside off, swinging away, seaming away, passing outside off (27% of deliveries).
  • Round the wicket to LHB 47% · over the wicket to RHB (round 0%).
  • Round the wicket he pitches fuller, up to 7.1 m.
  • Across an over he holds a fairly consistent length, banging it in more as the over goes on.

Biggest threats

  • Most dangerous length is Full (3 wkts, 4.1% adjusted strike).
  • Danger pitching line: Stumps (over the wicket).
  • Takes 17% of wickets pitching full on the 5th stump.
  • Beats the bat 8.3% of tracked balls (false-shot 23.5%).
  • Gets you bowled more than most — 25% of his wickets (1.3× the typical rate for this type).
  • 75% of catches are behind the wicket (keeper / slips / gully); most often to keeper, slip: 3rd, square leg: short leg.

Areas to exploit

  • Concedes most runs pitching back of a length wide outside off (20% of runs).
  • Short ball: 18% of deliveries, economy 4.6 — 2 wkts from 93 short balls.
  • Away from full, the wicket threat drops off — look to score in the less-productive lengths.
  • Most of the runs off them leak square/through the off side (54%) — their main scoring release.
  • Cash in when they go back of a length wide outside off (economy 8.3, beats the bat only 35%).

Solid line = career, dotted = last 3 years (where enough recent balls). Percentile within same-type peers (grey = the peer distribution, line = this bowler). Release/crease vs hand × pace/spin; movement/speed/repeatability vs pace/spin. Release & speed are modern-era (2017+ / partial). Crease variation = how much he moves his release point sideways across the crease from ball to ball (within his main angle): a high percentile = he varies where he lets the ball go a lot, a low percentile = he releases from the same spot every ball. Repeatability = length consistency over his stock-length band (2–11 m, so deliberate yorkers and bouncers don't count as poor control): a high percentile = tighter, more metronomic lengths than peers; a low percentile = he varies his length more. A marker at the very edge = he sits beyond the typical peer range on that trait.
